dimensions.assessment: Directly affects commercial fishing vessel operators, crewmembers, and organizations applying for safety and research grants.
dimensions.evidence: facing fishing vessel operators and crewmembers

dimensions.assessment: Expands training topics and research scope to cover substance use and fatigue, providing moderate financial support through competitive grants.
dimensions.evidence: conduct safety and prevention training that addresses behavioral and physical health risks, that include substance use disorder and worker fatigue

dimensions.assessment: Increases appropriations to the Secretary of Health and Human Services to $6,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029 for both training and research grant programs.
dimensions.evidence: for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029... $6,000,000

dimensions.assessment: Amends existing statutory provisions under title 46, United States Code, to broaden grant criteria and funding levels.
dimensions.evidence: Section 4502 of title 46, United States Code, is amended

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes specific funding levels annually across a five-year span from fiscal year 2025 through fiscal year 2029.
dimensions.evidence: for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029

missing_information: Long-term funding authorizations beyond fiscal year 2029
importance_detail.rationale: The bill amends fishing safety grant programs to include behavioral and physical health risks and increases authorized funding to $6 million annually for fiscal years 2025 through 2029.
